title: decree attention file frontmatter
description: The YAML frontmatter of a file decree writes in .decree/attention/, in one of two shapes by `kind`. `run`: .decree/attention/<id>.md, written when run <id> needs a person: it failed, was interrupted, waits in a `reply` state. `pause`: .decree/attention/pause.md, written by `decree pause`, which holds the queue until `decree resume` deletes it. A markdown body follows: what happened and the exact command that continues the run, or how to resume. The files are read-only: answer with `decree reply` or a reply, continue with `decree retry`. A `.md` file in the folder whose frontmatter is missing or does not match this schema holds the queue as if it had `holds: true`. Reference: docs/reference/cli.md, Attention.

run.description: A run that needs a person: .decree/attention/<run>.md.

kind.description: A run that needs a person.

run.description: The run's id; the file is `<run>.md`.

machine.description: The run's machine. A run with no machine of its own, the failed `invalid_message` run of a rejected reply, names the machine of the run the reply was addressed to; `machine` is absent when there is none (a reply to a run id that does not exist, or a message whose frontmatter names no machine).

status.description: `failed`: finished in `failed`. `interrupted`: stopped by a signal, or by a crash found later from a stale lock. `waiting`: waits in a `reply` state for a reply, which the body names.

state.description: The state the run is in; for a failed run, the state it failed from, which `decree retry` continues in.

since.description: When the run's status changed, RFC 3339 UTC: the `ts` of its last event.

holds.description: Whether the file holds the queue: the run has a `hold` file (written by the built-in `keep` script). While any file holds, `process` and `daemon` start and continue no runs.

pause.description: Written by `decree pause`: .decree/attention/pause.md. The runs going when it was written finish their current step loop; no run starts or continues until `decree resume` deletes it.

since.description: When `decree pause` wrote the file, RFC 3339 UTC; a later `decree pause` leaves it.

holds.description: The file always holds the queue.
